title: CaDRE: Controllable and Diverse Generation of Safety-Critical Driving Scenarios using Real-World Trajectories

control_signal.value: Desired values of user-defined measure functions (perturbation effort, normalised impact time, impact angle), used to ask for a specific scenario from the archive.

control_mechanism.value: Quality-Diversity black-box optimisation fills a discretised measure-space archive of bounded perturbations to real trajectories; control is retrieval of the stored scenario at the requested measure cell. Occupancy-aware restart improves exploration.

base_model.value: No learned generative model in packet: QD emitter (Gaussian sampling, CMA-style update) with a lightweight scenario simulator and a rule-based reactive ego policy; scenarios are acceleration/steering perturbations of one background vehicle.

datasets.value: Three scenarios selected from nuPlan v1.1: unprotected cross-turn, high-speed lane-change, U-turn; 15 s horizon each.

metrics.value: QD metrics: coverage (0-1), mean objective (0-1), QD score (max 4000, 10x20x20 grid). Objective f is collision with ego (1) or exp of minimum distance. Compared with RL and sampling baselines incl. SVPG.

controllability_evidence.value: Qualitative: in the cross-turn scenario, asking for different [m1,m2,m3] combinations retrieves a right-side hit or a left-side overtaking hit. No quantitative controllability number in packet.

stated_limitations.value: Some archive cells stay empty (infeasible measure combinations, e.g. short impact time with small impact angle in cross-turn); only one background vehicle is perturbed at a time.

notes: Optimisation-based, not a trained generator. Realism is argued by construction (bounded perturbation of real trajectories); no realism metric seen in packet. Limitations passage truncated.
